sections.title: 59.3 Security evaluation mathematics
sections.body:
Suppose we execute 500 representative adversarial test cases and observe:

| Outcome | Count |
|--------|--------|
| Attacks prevented | 485 |
| Security controls violated | 15 |
| Total tests | 500 |

Attack success rate:

\[
ASR=\frac{15}{500}\times100=3\%
\]

Defense success rate:

\[
DSR=\frac{485}{500}\times100=97\%
\]

These metrics must be calculated against precisely defined policy violations, not simply whether the model refused to answer.

sections.title: 59.4 False positive vs false negative
sections.body:
Illustrative security classifier confusion matrix | | Blocked | Allowed | |--------|--------|--------| | Malicious request | # 485

True positive | # 15

False negative | | Legitimate request | # 30

False positive | # 970

True negative | Detection precision: \[ Precision=\frac{485}{485+30}\approx94.17\% \] Detection recall: \[ Recall=\frac{485}{485+15}=97\% \] False-positive rate: \[ FPR=\frac{30}{30+970}=3\% \] These illustrative results show why injection detection alone is insufficient. Even a detector with high recall can miss malicious inputs. Independent execution authorization must prevent prohibited operations even when the detector fails. # Senior interview questions — Multi-agent security, MCP and A2A Target: senior AI engineers, lead engineers and AI architects with 8+ years of overall engineering experience. ### Q36. How would you implement zero trust in a multi-agent platform? Authenticate workload and user identities, enforce scoped delegation, validate every protected operation through an independent policy gateway and restrict access to specific resources. Do not trust an agent merely because it is deployed internally. ### Q37. What is the difference between an MCP gateway and an orchestration engine? The MCP gateway manages approved tool connectivity, protocol compatibility, security policies and invocation controls. The orchestration engine manages task planning, scheduling, dependency execution and lifecycle. They can be deployed together but serve different responsibilities. ### Q38. How would you manage 5,000 MCP tools without overflowing the context window? Filter tools according to permissions, retrieve relevant capabilities, rerank candidates and expose only a small compatible set. Evaluate required-tool Recall\@K so that context optimization does not remove necessary capabilities. ### Q39. How do you protect against MCP tool rug pulls? Maintain approved capability contracts, monitor metadata and schema changes, perform behavioral regression tests and suspend incompatible capabilities. A matching schema fingerprint does not guarantee unchanged behavior. ### Q40. Why is MCP token passthrough dangerous? A token intended for one resource may be incorrectly accepted or reused by another service. Validate token audience and obtain appropriately scoped downstream credentials through the supported authorization mechanism. ### Q41. How would you orchestrate agents implemented using different frameworks? Use compatible A2A adapters, approved Agent Cards, typed delegation contracts, authenticated workload identities and a durable orchestration ledger. The frameworks can maintain independent internal implementations. ### Q42. What happens if an A2A task is created remotely but its task reference is lost? Mark submission outcome as unknown. Reconcile using a durable logical delegation identity and compatible remote correlation mechanisms. Do not blindly resubmit consequential tasks. ### Q43. How do you prevent remote agents from exceeding their delegated permissions? Use scoped identities, resource restrictions, explicit delegation contracts and independent enforcement at the protected services. The parent's generated instructions are not sufficient authorization. ### Q44. What is inter-agent prompt injection? It occurs when untrusted instructions influence one agent and are propagated to other agents through messages, summaries, memory or artifacts. Preserve provenance, isolate context and independently enforce action permissions. ### Q45. What is instruction laundering in multi-agent systems? An untrusted instruction is transformed into an apparently legitimate recommendation or finding as it moves through agents. Mitigate it using source lineage, evidence verification and separation of recommendations from authorization. ### Q46. How do you prevent shared-memory poisoning? Classify memory candidates, verify authoritative claims, retain provenance, enforce scoped storage and support invalidation of dependent records. Never allow memory alone to grant permissions. ### Q47. How would you handle a compromised specialist agent? Suspend the affected version, revoke relevant capabilities, quarantine outputs, identify dependent workflows and reconcile external effects. Use a tested compatible replacement if necessary. ### Q48. Why is consensus among multiple LLM agents insufficient for security decisions? Their failures may be correlated. Agreement does not prove factual correctness or authorization. Use deterministic policies and independently verified business evidence. ### Q49. What is the confused deputy problem in multi-agent orchestration? A software component uses its legitimate elevated privileges to perform an operation that the requesting principal is not authorized to perform. Enforce both principal and acting workload identity, together with resource and purpose constraints. ### Q50. How do you sandbox a coding agent? Use restricted execution environments, filesystem isolation, resource quotas, network egress controls, limited credentials, execution deadlines and controlled artifact release. For hostile code, ordinary process or container isolation may be insufficient. ### Q51. How do you prevent SSRF in an agent with network-access capabilities? Restrict destinations through a trusted execution gateway, validate network destinations and redirects, and enforce controlled egress. Do not allow arbitrary model-generated URLs to bypass network policy. ### Q52. How do you design an emergency kill switch? Centrally revoke the affected capability, enforce revocation at protected gateways, stop new task admission, cancel eligible pending work and reconcile existing external operations. A system-prompt change alone is not a reliable kill switch. ### Q53. Can historical checkpoints safely restore authorization? No. Historical execution state may be restored, but current permissions, credential validity, revocations and approvals must be independently checked. ### Q54. How do you make agent audit records tamper-evident? Use protected append-only storage where appropriate, access separation, independently anchored digests or signatures, and checks for missing events. A standalone hash chain is insufficient if an attacker can rewrite the entire chain. ### Q55. How would you test the security of a production multi-agent platform? Use threat modeling, negative authorization tests, tenant-isolation tests, protocol contract tests, synthetic injection cases, concurrency tests, failure injection and verified external-state assertions. A successful security test proves that the prohibited effect was prevented, not merely that the model generated a refusal. # Enterprise multi-agent security readiness assessment ### Enterprise security assessment of 24 controls verified # % [Copy security checklist] Mark controls as verified only after obtaining implementation and testing evidence. # Current masterclass progress # 59 Numbered chapters covered # 35 Security scenarios analyzed # 55 / 100 Multi-agent interview Q&As # 20 New security test designs I extended this phase through Part 59 to accommodate the detailed security scenarios, incident case studies and testing laboratory.

sections.body:
Continuing from Part 59, where we completed advanced MCP, A2A, zero-trust architecture, 35 security scenarios and adversarial testing.

In this phase, we will learn how to operate multi-agent systems under real production constraints: thousands of concurrent tasks, limited provider quotas, shared financial budgets, unreliable dependencies, distributed workers and unpredictable model behavior.

All example costs, provider limits and performance measurements are hypothetical unless explicitly stated otherwise.
